notes: Names are full firmware parameter names — never prefix-stripped (BATT_MONITOR, not MONITOR).
default is null: ArduPilot parameter metadata does not publish defaults (they are vehicle/board specific). null means unknown, not zero.
type: 'enum' and 'bitmask' come from upstream @Values / @Bitmask and are authoritative. 'float' means numeric whose exact storage type is not stated.
description is the upstream @Description for this exact parameter — no offset, no @PREFIX@ placeholders.

parameters.name: ACRO_BAL_PITCH
parameters.description: rate at which pitch angle returns to level in acro and sport mode.  A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster. For helicopter sets the decay rate of the virtual flybar in the pitch axis. A higher value causes faster decay of desired to actual attitude.

parameters.name: ACRO_BAL_ROLL
parameters.description: rate at which roll angle returns to level in acro and sport mode.  A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster. For helicopter sets the decay rate of the virtual flybar in the roll axis. A higher value causes faster decay of desired to actual attitude.

parameters.name: ACRO_OPTIONS
parameters.description: A range of options that can be applied to change acro mode behaviour. Air-mode enables ATC_THR_MIX_MAN at all times (air-mode has no effect on helicopters). Rate Loop Only disables the use of angle stabilization and uses angular rate stabilization only.

parameters.name: ACRO_RP_EXPO
parameters.description: Acro roll/pitch Expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

parameters.name: ACRO_RP_P
parameters.display_name: Acro Roll and Pitch P gain
parameters.description: Converts pilot roll and pitch into a desired rate of rotation in ACRO and SPORT mode.  Higher values mean faster rate of rotation.

parameters.name: ACRO_THR_MID
parameters.description: Acro Throttle Mid

parameters.name: ACRO_TRAINER
parameters.description: Type of trainer used in acro mode

parameters.name: ACRO_YAW_P
parameters.description: Converts pilot yaw input into a desired rate of rotation.  Higher values mean faster rate of rotation.

parameters.name: ACRO_Y_EXPO
parameters.description: Acro yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

parameters.name: ADSB_EMIT_TYPE
parameters.description: ADSB classification for the type of vehicle emitting the transponder signal. Default value is 14 (UAV).

parameters.name: ADSB_ICAO_ID
parameters.description: ICAO_ID unique vehicle identification number of this aircraft. This is a integer limited to 24bits. If set to 0 then one will be randomly generated. If set to -1 then static information is not sent, transceiver is assumed pre-programmed.

parameters.name: ADSB_ICAO_SPECL
parameters.description: ICAO_ID of special vehicle that ignores ADSB_LIST_RADIUS and ADSB_LIST_ALT. The vehicle is always tracked. Use 0 to disable.

parameters.name: ADSB_LEN_WIDTH
parameters.description: Aircraft length and width dimension options in Length and Width in meters. In most cases, use a value of 1 for smallest size.

parameters.name: ADSB_LIST_ALT
parameters.description: ADSB vehicle list altitude filter. Vehicles detected above this altitude will be completely ignored. They will not show up in the SRx_ADSB stream to the GCS and will not be considered in any avoidance calculations. A value of 0 will disable this filter.

parameters.name: ADSB_LIST_MAX
parameters.description: ADSB list size of nearest vehicles. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.

parameters.name: ADSB_LIST_RADIUS
parameters.description: ADSB vehicle list radius filter. Vehicles detected outside this radius will be completely ignored. They will not show up in the SRx_ADSB stream to the GCS and will not be considered in any avoidance calculations. A value of 0 will disable this filter.

parameters.name: ADSB_LOG
parameters.description: 0: no logging, 1: log only special ID, 2:log all

parameters.name: ADSB_OFFSET_LAT
parameters.description: GPS antenna lateral offset. This describes the physical location offest from center of the GPS antenna on the aircraft.

parameters.name: ADSB_OFFSET_LON
parameters.description: GPS antenna longitudinal offset. This is usually set to 1, Applied By Sensor

parameters.name: ADSB_RF_CAPABLE
parameters.description: Describes your hardware RF In/Out capabilities.

parameters.name: ADSB_RF_SELECT
parameters.description: Transceiver RF selection for Rx enable and/or Tx enable. This only effects devices that can Tx and/or Rx. Rx-only devices should override this to always be Rx-only.

parameters.name: ADSB_SQUAWK
parameters.description: VFR squawk (Mode 3/A) code is a pre-programmed default code when the pilot is flying VFR and not in contact with ATC. In the USA, the VFR squawk code is octal 1200 (hex 0x280, decimal 640) and in most parts of Europe the VFR squawk code is octal 7000. If an invalid octal number is set then it will be reset to 1200.

parameters.name: ADSB_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of ADS-B hardware for ADSB-in and ADSB-out configuration and operation. If any type is selected then MAVLink based ADSB-in messages will always be enabled

parameters.name: AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS
parameters.display_name: Error margin for GPS based AMSL limit
parameters.description: This sets margin for error in GPS derived altitude limit. This error margin is only used if the barometer has failed. If the barometer fails then the GPS will be used to enforce the AMSL_LIMIT, but this margin will be subtracted from the AMSL_LIMIT first, to ensure that even with the given amount of GPS altitude error the pressure altitude is not breached. OBC users should set this to comply with their D2 safety case. A value of -1 will mean that barometer failure will lead to immediate termination.

parameters.name: AFS_AMSL_LIMIT
parameters.description: This sets the AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude limit. If the pressure altitude determined by QNH exceeds this limit then flight termination will be forced. Note that this limit is in meters, whereas pressure altitude limits are often quoted in feet. A value of zero disables the pressure altitude limit.

parameters.name: AFS_DUAL_LOSS
parameters.display_name: Enable dual loss terminate due to failure of both GCS and GPS simultaneously
parameters.description: This enables the dual loss termination part of the AFS system. If this parameter is 1 and both GPS and the ground control station fail simultaneously, this will be considered a "dual loss" and cause termination.

parameters.name: AFS_ENABLE
parameters.description: This enables the advanced failsafe system. If this is set to zero (disable) then all the other AFS options have no effect

parameters.name: AFS_GEOFENCE
parameters.description: This enables the geofence part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

parameters.name: AFS_HB_PIN
parameters.description: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination.

parameters.name: AFS_MAN_PIN
parameters.description: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode

parameters.name: AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of comms loss events
parameters.description: Maximum number of comms loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on comms recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of comms loss events.

parameters.name: AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of GPS loss events
parameters.description: Maximum number of GPS loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on GPS recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of GPS loss events.

parameters.name: AFS_MAX_RANGE
parameters.description: This is the maximum range of the vehicle in kilometers from first arming. If the vehicle goes beyond this range then the TERM_ACTION is performed. A value of zero disables this feature.

parameters.name: AFS_QNH_PRESSURE
parameters.description: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.

parameters.name: AFS_RC
parameters.description: This enables the RC part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

parameters.name: AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME
parameters.description: This is the time in seconds in manual mode that failsafe termination will activate if RC input is lost. For the OBC rules this should be (1.5). Use 0 to disable.

parameters.name: AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY
parameters.display_name: Enable RC Termination only in manual control modes
parameters.description: If this parameter is set to 1, then an RC loss will only cause the plane to terminate in manual control modes. If it is 0, then the plane will terminate in any flight mode.

parameters.name: AFS_TERMINATE
parameters.description: Can be set in flight to force termination of the heartbeat signal

parameters.name: AFS_TERM_ACTION
parameters.description: This can be used to force an action on flight termination. Normally this is handled by an external failsafe board, but you can setup ArduPilot to handle it here. Please consult the wiki for more information on the possible values of the parameter

parameters.name: AFS_TERM_PIN
parameters.description: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination

parameters.name: AFS_WP_COMMS
parameters.description: Waypoint number to navigate to on comms loss

parameters.name: AFS_WP_GPS_LOSS
parameters.description: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss

parameters.name: AHRS_COMP_BETA
parameters.display_name: AHRS Velocity Complementary Filter Beta Coefficient
parameters.description: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.

parameters.name: AHRS_CUSTOM_PIT
parameters.description: Autopilot mounting position pitch offset. Positive values = pitch up, negative values = pitch down. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL
parameters.description: Autopilot mounting position roll offset. Positive values = roll right, negative values = roll left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: AHRS_CUSTOM_YAW
parameters.description: Autopilot mounting position yaw offset. Positive values = yaw right, negative values = yaw left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.

parameters.name: AHRS_EKF_TYPE
parameters.display_name: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation
parameters.description: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation

parameters.name: AHRS_GPS_GAIN
parameters.description: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.

parameters.name: AHRS_GPS_MINSATS
parameters.description: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.

parameters.name: AHRS_GPS_USE
parameters.description: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS whenever it is available.

parameters.name: AHRS_ORIENTATION
parameters.description: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle.

parameters.name: AHRS_RP_P
parameters.description: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

parameters.name: AHRS_TRIM_X
parameters.description: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.

parameters.name: AHRS_TRIM_Y
parameters.description: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

parameters.name: AHRS_TRIM_Z
parameters.description: Not Used

parameters.name: AHRS_WIND_MAX
parameters.description: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is. See ARSPD_OPTIONS and ARSPD_MAX_WIND to disable airspeed sensors.

parameters.name: AHRS_YAW_P
parameters.description: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.

parameters.name: ANGLE_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum lean angle in all flight modes

parameters.name: ARMING_ACCTHRESH
parameters.description: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.

parameters.name: ARMING_CHECK
parameters.description: Checks prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks that will be performed before allowing arming. For most users it is recommended to leave this at the default of 1 (all checks enabled). You can select whatever checks you prefer by adding together the values of each check type to set this parameter. For example, to only allow arming when you have GPS lock and no RC failsafe you would set ARMING_CHECK to 72.

parameters.name: ARMING_MIS_ITEMS
parameters.description: Bitmask of mission items that are required to be planned in order to arm the aircraft

parameters.name: ARMING_RUDDER
parameters.description: Allow arm/disarm by rudder input. When enabled arming can be done with right rudder, disarming with left rudder. Rudder arming only works in manual throttle modes with throttle at zero +- deadzone (RCx_DZ)

parameters.name: AROT_AS_ACC_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum forward acceleration to apply in speed controller.

parameters.name: AROT_BAIL_TIME
parameters.description: Time in seconds from bail out initiated to the exit of autorotation flight mode.

parameters.name: AROT_COL_FILT_E
parameters.description: Cut-off frequency for collective low pass filter.  For the entry phase.  Acts as a following trim.  Must be higher than AROT_COL_FILT_G.

parameters.name: AROT_COL_FILT_G
parameters.description: Cut-off frequency for collective low pass filter.  For the glide phase.  Acts as a following trim.  Must be lower than AROT_COL_FILT_E.

parameters.name: AROT_ENABLE
parameters.description: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the autonomous autorotation capability.

parameters.name: AROT_FW_V_FF
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) input filter.  Corrects the target acceleration proportionally to the desired velocity.

parameters.name: AROT_FW_V_P
parameters.description: Velocity (horizontal) P gain.  Determines the propotion of the target acceleration based on the velocity error.

parameters.name: AROT_HS_P
parameters.display_name: P gain for head speed controller
parameters.description: Increase value to increase sensitivity of head speed controller during autonomous autorotation.

parameters.name: AROT_HS_SENSOR
parameters.description: Allocate the RPM sensor instance to use for measuring head speed.  RPM1 = 0.  RPM2 = 1.

parameters.name: AROT_HS_SET_PT
parameters.description: The target head speed in RPM during autorotation.  Start by setting to desired hover speed and tune from there as necessary.

parameters.name: AROT_TARG_SP
parameters.description: Target ground speed in cm/s for the autorotation controller to try and achieve/ maintain during the glide phase.

parameters.description: Maximum acceleration in pitch axis

parameters.name: ATC_ACCEL_R_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum acceleration in roll axis

parameters.name: ATC_ACCEL_Y_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum acceleration in yaw axis

parameters.name: ATC_ANGLE_BOOST
parameters.description: Angle Boost increases output throttle as the vehicle leans to reduce loss of altitude

parameters.name: ATC_ANG_LIM_TC
parameters.display_name: Angle Limit (to maintain altitude) Time Constant
parameters.description: Angle Limit (to maintain altitude) Time Constant

parameters.name: ATC_ANG_PIT_P
parameters.display_name: Pitch axis angle controller P gain
parameters.description: Pitch axis angle controller P gain.  Converts the error between the desired pitch angle and actual angle to a desired pitch rate

parameters.name: ATC_ANG_RLL_P
parameters.display_name: Roll axis angle controller P gain
parameters.description: Roll axis angle controller P gain.  Converts the error between the desired roll angle and actual angle to a desired roll rate

parameters.name: ATC_ANG_YAW_P
parameters.display_name: Yaw axis angle controller P gain

parameters.name: ATC_HOVR_ROL_TRM
parameters.description: Trim the hover roll angle to counter tail rotor thrust in a hover

parameters.name: ATC_INPUT_TC
parameters.description: Attitude control input time constant.  Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

parameters.name: ATC_PIRO_COMP
parameters.description: Pirouette compensation enabled

parameters.name: ATC_RATE_FF_ENAB
parameters.description: Controls whether body-frame rate feedfoward is enabled or disabled

parameters.name: ATC_RATE_P_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum angular velocity in pitch axis

parameters.name: ATC_RATE_R_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum angular velocity in roll axis

parameters.name: ATC_RATE_Y_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum angular velocity in yaw axis

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_D
parameters.display_name: Pitch axis rate controller D gain
parameters.description: Pitch axis rate controller D gain.  Compensates for short-term change in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_FF
parameters.display_name: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward
parameters.description: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward

parameters.description: Pitch axis rate controller target frequency in Hz

parameters.display_name: Pitch axis rate controller I gain
parameters.description: Pitch axis rate controller I gain.  Corrects long-term difference in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_ILMI
parameters.display_name: Pitch axis rate controller I-term leak minimum
parameters.description: Point below which I-term will not leak down

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_IMAX
parameters.display_name: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum
parameters.description: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum.  Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_P
parameters.display_name: Pitch axis rate controller P gain
parameters.description: Pitch axis rate controller P gain.  Converts the difference between desired pitch rate and actual pitch rate into a motor speed output

parameters.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_SMAX
parameters.description: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

parameters.name: ATC_SLEW_YAW
parameters.description: Maximum rate the yaw target can be updated in Loiter, RTL, Auto flight modes

parameters.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MAN
parameters.description: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during manual flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

parameters.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MAX
parameters.description: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during active flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

parameters.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MIN
parameters.description: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used when landing (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_AGGR
parameters.description: Autotune aggressiveness. Defines the bounce back used to detect size of the D term.

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_AXES
parameters.description: 1-byte bitmap of axes to autotune

parameters.name: AUTOTUNE_MIN_D
parameters.description: Defines the minimum D gain

parameters.name: AUTO_OPTIONS
parameters.description: A range of options that can be applied to change auto mode behaviour. Allow Arming allows the copter to be armed in Auto. Allow Takeoff Without Raising Throttle allows takeoff without the pilot having to raise the throttle. Ignore pilot yaw overrides the pilot's yaw stick being used while in auto.

parameters.name: AVD_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable Avoidance using ADSB

parameters.name: AVD_F_ACTION
parameters.description: Specifies aircraft behaviour when a collision is imminent

parameters.name: AVD_F_ALT_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude for ADS-B avoidance. If the vehicle is below this altitude, no avoidance action will take place. Useful to prevent ADS-B avoidance from activating while below the tree line or around structures. Default of 0 is no minimum.

parameters.name: AVD_F_DIST_XY
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before F_ACTION is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_F_DIST_Z
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before BEHAVIOUR_F is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_F_RCVRY
parameters.display_name: Recovery behaviour after a fail event
parameters.description: Determines what the aircraft will do after a fail event is resolved

parameters.name: AVD_F_TIME
parameters.description: Aircraft velocity vectors are multiplied by this time to determine closest approach.  If this results in an approach closer than F_DIST_XY or F_DIST_Z then F_ACTION is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_OBS_MAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of obstacles to track
parameters.description: Maximum number of obstacles to track

parameters.name: AVD_W_ACTION
parameters.description: Specifies aircraft behaviour when a collision may occur

parameters.name: AVD_W_DIST_XY
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before W_ACTION is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_W_DIST_Z
parameters.description: Closest allowed projected distance before BEHAVIOUR_W is undertaken

parameters.name: AVD_W_TIME
parameters.description: Aircraft velocity vectors are multiplied by this time to determine closest approach.  If this results in an approach closer than W_DIST_XY or W_DIST_Z then W_ACTION is undertaken (assuming F_ACTION is not undertaken)

parameters.name: AVOID_ACCEL_MAX
parameters.description: Maximum acceleration with which obstacles will be avoided with. Set zero to disable acceleration limits

parameters.name: AVOID_ALT_MIN
parameters.description: Minimum altitude above which proximity based avoidance will start working. This requires a valid downward facing rangefinder reading to work. Set zero to disable

parameters.name: AVOID_ANGLE_MAX
parameters.display_name: Avoidance max lean angle in non-GPS flight modes
parameters.description: Max lean angle used to avoid obstacles while in non-GPS modes

parameters.name: AVOID_BACKUP_DZ
parameters.display_name: Avoidance deadzone between stopping and backing away from obstacle
parameters.description: Distance beyond AVOID_MARGIN parameter, after which vehicle will backaway from obstacles. Increase this parameter if you see vehicle going back and forth in front of obstacle.

parameters.name: AVOID_BACKUP_SPD
parameters.description: Maximum speed that will be used to back away from obstacles in GPS modes (m/s). Set zero to disable

parameters.name: AVOID_BEHAVE
parameters.description: Avoidance behaviour (slide or stop)

parameters.name: AVOID_DIST_MAX
parameters.display_name: Avoidance distance maximum in non-GPS flight modes
parameters.description: Distance from object at which obstacle avoidance will begin in non-GPS modes

parameters.name: AVOID_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enabled/disable avoidance input sources

parameters.name: AVOID_MARGIN
parameters.display_name: Avoidance distance margin in GPS modes
parameters.description: Vehicle will attempt to stay at least this distance (in meters) from objects while in GPS modes

parameters.name: BARO1_DEVID
parameters.description: Barometer sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

parameters.name: BARO1_GND_PRESS
parameters.description: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

parameters.name: BARO1_WCF_BCK
parameters.display_name: Pressure error coefficient in negative X direction (backwards)

parameters.name: BARO_ALT_OFFSET
parameters.description: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.

parameters.name: BARO_EXT_BUS
parameters.description: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the GND_PROBE_EXT parameter.

parameters.name: BARO_FLTR_RNG
parameters.display_name: Range in which sample is accepted
parameters.description: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

parameters.name: BARO_GND_TEMP
parameters.description: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.

parameters.name: BARO_PRIMARY
parameters.description: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found

parameters.name: BARO_PROBE_EXT
parameters.description: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on GND_EXT_BUS. If BARO_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in GND_EXT_BUS.

parameters.name: BARO_SPEC_GRAV
parameters.description: This sets the specific gravity of the fluid when flying an underwater ROV.

parameters.name: BATT2_AMP_OFFSET
parameters.description: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

parameters.name: BATT2_AMP_PERVLT
parameters.description: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. With a Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17.

parameters.name: BATT2_ARM_MAH
parameters.description: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATT2__ARM_VOLT parameter.

parameters.name: BATT2_ARM_VOLT
parameters.description: Battery voltage level which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any voltage.

parameters.name: BATT2_BUS
parameters.description: Battery monitor I2C bus number

parameters.name: BATT2_CAPACITY
parameters.description: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

parameters.name: BATT2_CRT_MAH
parameters.description: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2__FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

parameters.name: BATT2_CRT_VOLT
parameters.description: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

parameters.name: BATT2_CURR_PIN
parameters.description: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for current monitoring.

parameters.name: BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT
parameters.description: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a critical battery failsafe

parameters.name: BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT
parameters.description: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe

parameters.name: BATT2_FS_VOLTSRC
parameters.description: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event

parameters.name: BATT2_LOW_MAH
parameters.description: Battery capacity at which the low battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

parameters.name: BATT2_LOW_TIMER
parameters.description: This is the timeout in seconds before a low voltage event will be triggered. For aircraft with low C batteries it may be necessary to raise this in order to cope with low voltage on long takeoffs. A value of zero disables low voltage errors.

parameters.name: BATT2_LOW_VOLT
parameters.description: Battery voltage that triggers a low battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

parameters.description: IMU Heater integrator maximum

parameters.name: BRD_IO_ENABLE
parameters.description: This allows for the IO co-processor on FMUv1 and FMUv2 to be disabled

parameters.name: BRD_OPTIONS

parameters.description: Controls number of FMU outputs which are setup for PWM. All unassigned pins can be used for GPIO

parameters.name: BRD_PWM_VOLT_SEL
parameters.description: This sets the voltage max for PWM output pulses. 0 for 3.3V and 1 for 5V output.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_ABLVL
parameters.description: This sets the minimum RSSI of an auto-bind packet for it to be accepted. This should be set so that auto-bind will only happen at short range to minimise the change of an auto-bind happening accidentially

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_ABTIME
parameters.description: When non-zero this sets the time with no transmitter packets before we start looking for auto-bind packets.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_BZOFS
parameters.description: Set transmitter buzzer note adjustment (adjust frequency up)

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_DEBUG
parameters.description: radio debug level

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_DISCRC
parameters.description: disable receive CRC (for debug)

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_FCCTST
parameters.display_name: Put radio into FCC test mode
parameters.description: If this is enabled then the radio will continuously transmit as required for FCC testing. The transmit channel is set by the value of the parameter. The radio will not work for RC input while this is enabled

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_PPSCH
parameters.description: Channel to show received packet-per-second rate, or zero for disabled

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_PROT
parameters.description: Select air protocol

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_SIGCH
parameters.description: Channel to show receive RSSI signal strength, or zero for disabled

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_STKMD
parameters.description: This selects between different stick input modes. The default is mode2, which has throttle on the left stick and pitch on the right stick. You can instead set mode1, which has throttle on the right stick and pitch on the left stick.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TELEM
parameters.description: If this is non-zero then telemetry packets will be sent over DSM

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TESTCH
parameters.display_name: Set radio to factory test channel
parameters.description: This sets the radio to a fixed test channel for factory testing. Using a fixed channel avoids the need for binding in factory testing.

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TPPSCH
parameters.description: Channel to show telemetry packets-per-second value, as received at TX

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TSIGCH

parameters.description: Channel to show telemetry RSSI value as received by TX

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TXMAX
parameters.description: Set transmitter maximum transmit power (from 1 to 8)

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TXPOW
parameters.description: Set telemetry transmit power. This is the power level (from 1 to 8) for telemetry packets sent from the RX to the TX

parameters.name: BRD_RADIO_TYPE
parameters.display_name: Set type of direct attached radio
parameters.description: This enables support for direct attached radio receivers

parameters.name: BRD_RTC_TYPES
parameters.description: Specifies which sources of UTC time will be accepted

parameters.name: BRD_RTC_TZ_MIN
parameters.description: Adds offset in +- minutes from UTC to calculate local time

parameters.name: BRD_SAFETYENABLE
parameters.display_name: Enable use of safety arming switch
parameters.description: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.

parameters.name: BRD_SAFETYOPTION
parameters.description: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed

bitmask.3: Force safety on when the aircraft disarms

parameters.name: BRD_SAFETY_MASK
parameters.display_name: Outputs which ignore the safety switch state
parameters.description: A bitmask which controls what outputs can move while the safety switch has not been pressed

parameters.name: BRD_SBUS_OUT
parameters.description: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz

parameters.name: BRD_SD_SLOWDOWN
parameters.description: This is a scaling factor to slow down microSD operation. It can be used on flight board and microSD card combinations where full speed is not reliable. For normal full speed operation a value of 0 should be used.

parameters.name: BRD_SER1_RTSCTS
parameters.description: Enable flow control on serial 1 (telemetry 1) on Pixhawk. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. Note that the PX4v1 does not have hardware flow control pins on this port, so you should leave this disabled.

parameters.name: BRD_SER2_RTSCTS

The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

parameters.name: BRD_SER3_RTSCTS

If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

parameters.name: BRD_SER4_RTSCTS

If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

parameters.name: BRD_SER5_RTSCTS

If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

parameters.description: pin number to use for save accurate camera feedback messages. If set to -1 then don't use a pin flag for this, otherwise this is a pin number which if held high after a picture trigger order, will save camera messages when camera really takes a picture. A universal camera hot shoe is needed. The pin should be held high for at least 2 milliseconds for reliable trigger detection. See also the CAM_FEEDBACK_POL option.

parameters.description: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the feedback pin should go high on trigger. If set to 0 then it should go low

parameters.name: CAM_RC_MDE_DELAY

parameters.description: Time it takes for the a RunCam mode button press to be actived in ms. If a mode change first requires a video recording change then double this value is used. If this is too short then commands can get out of sync.

parameters.description: Setting this to Enabled(1) will enable the compass. Setting this to Disabled(0) will disable the compass. Note that this is separate from COMPASS_USE. This will enable the low level senor, and will enable logging of magnetometer data. To use the compass for navigation you must also set COMPASS_USE to 1.

parameters.name: COMPASS_EXTERN2
parameters.display_name: Compass2 is attached via an external cable
parameters.description: Configure second compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

parameters.name: COMPASS_EXTERN3
parameters.display_name: Compass3 is attached via an external cable
parameters.description: Configure third compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

parameters.name: COMPASS_EXTERNAL
parameters.display_name: Compass is attached via an external cable
parameters.description: Configure compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. Set to 1 if the compass is externally connected. When externally connected the COMPASS_ORIENT option operates independently of the AHRS_ORIENTATION board orientation option. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

parameters.name: COMPASS_FLTR_RNG
parameters.display_name: Range in which sample is accepted
parameters.description: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

parameters.name: COMPASS_LEARN
parameters.description: Enable or disable the automatic learning of compass offsets. You can enable learning either using a compass-only method that is suitable only for fixed wing aircraft or using the offsets learnt by the active EKF state estimator. If this option is enabled then the learnt offsets are saved when you disarm the vehicle. If InFlight learning is enabled then the compass with automatically start learning once a flight starts (must be armed). While InFlight learning is running you cannot use position control modes.

parameters.name: COMPASS_OPTIONS
parameters.description: This sets options to change the behaviour of the compass

parameters.name: COMPASS_ORIENT
parameters.description: The orientation of the first external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used.

parameters.name: COMPASS_ORIENT2
parameters.description: The orientation of a second external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used.

parameters.name: COMPASS_ORIENT3
parameters.description: The orientation of a third external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used.

parameters.description: Delay before automatic disarm in seconds. A value of zero disables auto disarm.

parameters.name: EAHRS_RATE
parameters.description: Requested rate for AHRS device

parameters.name: EAHRS_TYPE
parameters.description: Type of AHRS device

parameters.name: EK2_ABIAS_P_NSE
parameters.description: This noise controls the growth of the vertical accelerometer delta velocity bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes accelerometer bias estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK2_ACC_P_NSE
parameters.description: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to accelerometer measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the accelerometer measurements less and other measurements more.

parameters.name: EK2_ALT_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors.

parameters.name: EK2_ALT_SOURCE
parameters.description: Primary height sensor used by the EKF. If a sensor other than Baro is selected and becomes unavailable, then the Baro sensor will be used as a fallback. NOTE: The EK2_RNG_USE_HGT parameter can be used to switch to range-finder when close to the ground in conjunction with EK2_ALT_SOURCE = 0 or 2 (Baro or GPS).

parameters.name: EK2_BCN_DELAY
parameters.description: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.

parameters.name: EK2_BCN_I_GTE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_BCN_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

parameters.name: EK2_CHECK_SCALE
parameters.description: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.

parameters.name: EK2_EAS_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the airspeed measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_EAS_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in equivalent airspeed measurements used by planes. Increasing it reduces the weighting of airspeed measurements and will make wind speed estimates less noisy and slower to converge. Increasing also increases navigation errors when dead-reckoning without GPS measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_ENABLE
parameters.description: This enables EKF2. Enabling EKF2 only makes the maths run, it does not mean it will be used for flight control. To use it for flight control set AHRS_EKF_TYPE=2. A reboot or restart will need to be performed after changing the value of EK2_ENABLE for it to take effect.

parameters.name: EK2_FLOW_DELAY
parameters.description: This is the number of msec that the optical flow measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.

parameters.name: EK2_FLOW_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the optical flow innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_FLOW_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise and errors in optical flow measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_FLOW_USE
parameters.description: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.

parameters.name: EK2_GBIAS_P_NSE
parameters.description: This state  process noise controls growth of the gyro delta angle bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes rate gyro bias estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK2_GLITCH_RAD
parameters.description: This controls the maximum radial uncertainty in position between the value predicted by the filter and the value measured by the GPS before the filter position and velocity states are reset to the GPS. Making this value larger allows the filter to ignore larger GPS glitches but also means that non-GPS errors such as IMU and compass can create a larger error in position before the filter is forced back to the GPS position.

parameters.name: EK2_GPS_CHECK
parameters.description: This is a 1 byte bitmap controlling which GPS preflight checks are performed. Set to 0 to bypass all checks. Set to 255 perform all checks. Set to 3 to check just the number of satellites and HDoP. Set to 31 for the most rigorous checks that will still allow checks to pass when the copter is moving, eg launch from a boat.

parameters.name: EK2_GPS_TYPE
parameters.description: This controls use of GPS measurements : 0 = use 3D velocity & 2D position, 1 = use 2D velocity and 2D position, 2 = use 2D position, 3 = Inhibit GPS use - this can be useful when flying with an optical flow sensor in an environment where GPS quality is poor and subject to large multipath errors.

parameters.name: EK2_GSCL_P_NSE
parameters.description: This noise controls the rate of gyro scale factor learning. Increasing it makes rate gyro scale factor estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK2_GSF_RST_MAX
parameters.display_name: Maximum number of resets to the EKF-GSF yaw estimate allowed
parameters.description: Sets the maximum number of times the EKF2 will be allowed to reset it's yaw to the estimate from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator. No resets will be allowed unless the use of the EKF-GSF yaw estimate is enabled via the EK2_GSF_USE parameter.

parameters.name: EK2_GSF_RUN_MASK
parameters.display_name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run
parameters.description: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF2 instances run an independant EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF2 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK2_GSF_USE, EK2_GSF_DELAY and EK2_GSF_MAXCOUNT parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK2_GSF_USE to 0.

parameters.name: EK2_GSF_USE_MASK
parameters.display_name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators are used
parameters.description: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF2 instances will use the output from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator that has been turned on by the EK2_GSF_RUN parameter. If the inertial navigation calculation stops following the GPS, then the vehicle code can request EKF2 to attempt to resolve the issue, either by performing a yaw reset if enabled by this parameter by switching to another EKF2 instance. Additionally the EKF2 will  initiate a reset internally if navigation is lost for more than EK2_GSF_DELAY milli seconds.

parameters.name: EK2_GYRO_P_NSE
parameters.description: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to gyro measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the gyro measurements less and other measurements more.

parameters.name: EK2_HGT_DELAY
parameters.description: This is the number of msec that the Height measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_HGT_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the height measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_HRT_FILT
parameters.description: Specifies the crossover frequency of the complementary filter used to calculate the output predictor height rate derivative.

parameters.name: EK2_IMU_MASK
parameters.description: 1 byte bitmap of IMUs to use in EKF2. A separate instance of EKF2 will be started for each IMU selected. Set to 1 to use the first IMU only (default), set to 2 to use the second IMU only, set to 3 to use the first and second IMU. Additional IMU's can be used up to a maximum of 6 if memory and processing resources permit. There may be insufficient memory and processing resources to run multiple instances. If this occurs EKF2 will fail to start.

parameters.name: EK2_MAGB_P_NSE
parameters.description: This state process noise controls the growth of body magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes magnetometer bias error estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK2_MAGE_P_NSE
parameters.description: This state process noise controls the growth of earth magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes earth magnetic field estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK2_MAG_CAL
parameters.description: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states, when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states and when it will use an alternative method of yaw determination to the magnetometer. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK2_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK2_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK2_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK2_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK2_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK2_MAG_MASK parameter. NOTE: limited operation without a magnetometer or any other yaw sensor is possible by setting all COMPASS_USE, COMPASS_USE2, COMPASS_USE3, etc parameters to 0 with COMPASS_ENABLE set to 1. If this is done, the EK2_GSF_RUN and EK2_GSF_USE masks must be set to the same as EK2_IMU_MASK.

parameters.name: EK2_MAG_EF_LIM
parameters.description: This limits the difference between the learned earth magnetic field and the earth field from the world magnetic model tables. A value of zero means to disable the use of the WMM tables.

parameters.name: EK2_MAG_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_MAG_MASK
parameters.display_name: Bitmask of active EKF cores that will always use heading fusion
parameters.description: 1 byte bitmap of EKF cores that will disable magnetic field states and use simple magnetic heading fusion at all times. This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.

parameters.name: EK2_MAG_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in magnetometer measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_MAX_FLOW
parameters.description: This sets the magnitude maximum optical flow rate in rad/sec that will be accepted by the filter

parameters.name: EK2_NOAID_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets the amount of position variation that the EKF allows for when operating without external measurements (eg GPS or optical flow). Increasing this parameter makes the EKF attitude estimate less sensitive to vehicle manoeuvres but more sensitive to IMU errors.

parameters.name: EK2_OGN_HGT_MASK
parameters.display_name: Bitmask control of EKF reference height correction
parameters.description: When a height sensor other than GPS is used as the primary height source by the EKF, the position of the zero height datum is defined by that sensor and its frame of reference. If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).

bitmask.1: Correct when using range finder height

parameters.name: EK2_POSNE_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets the GPS horizontal position observation noise. Increasing it reduces the weighting of GPS horizontal position measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_POS_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS position measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_RNG_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range finder innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_RNG_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in the range finder measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

parameters.name: EK2_RNG_USE_HGT
parameters.description: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFND_MAX_CM). This will not work unless Baro or GPS height is selected as the primary height source vis EK2_ALT_SOURCE = 0 or 2 respectively.  This feature should not be used for terrain following as it is designed  for vertical takeoff and landing with climb above  the range finder use height before commencing the mission, and with horizontal position changes below that height being limited to a flat region around the takeoff and landing point.

parameters.name: EK2_RNG_USE_SPD
parameters.description: The range finder will not be used as the primary height source when the horizontal ground speed is greater than this value.

parameters.name: EK2_TAU_OUTPUT
parameters.description: Sets the time constant of the output complementary filter/predictor in centi-seconds.

parameters.name: EK2_TERR_GRAD
parameters.description: Specifies the maximum gradient of the terrain below the vehicle assumed when it is fusing range finder or optical flow to estimate terrain height.

parameters.name: EK2_VELD_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set vertical velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS vertical velocity measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_VELNE_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set horizontal velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS horizontal velocity measurements.

parameters.name: EK2_VEL_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements willbe rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_WIND_PSCALE
parameters.display_name: Height rate to wind process noise scaler
parameters.description: This controls how much the process noise on the wind states is increased when gaining or losing altitude to take into account changes in wind speed and direction with altitude. Increasing this parameter increases how rapidly the wind states adapt when changing altitude, but does make wind velocity estimation noiser.

parameters.name: EK2_WIND_P_NSE
parameters.description: This state process noise controls the growth of wind state error estimates. Increasing it makes wind estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK2_YAW_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK2_YAW_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

parameters.name: EK3_ABIAS_P_NSE
parameters.description: This noise controls the growth of the vertical accelerometer delta velocity bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes accelerometer bias estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK3_ACC_BIAS_LIM
parameters.description: The accelerometer bias state will be limited to +- this value

parameters.name: EK3_ACC_P_NSE
parameters.description: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to accelerometer measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the accelerometer measurements less and other measurements more.

parameters.name: EK3_AFFINITY
parameters.description: These options control the affinity between sensor instances and EKF cores

parameters.name: EK3_ALT_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors.

parameters.name: EK3_BCN_DELAY
parameters.description: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.

parameters.name: EK3_BCN_I_GTE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK3_BCN_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

parameters.name: EK3_BETA_MASK
parameters.description: 1 byte bitmap controlling use of sideslip angle fusion for estimation of non wind states during operation of 'fly forward' vehicle types such as fixed wing planes. By assuming that the angle of sideslip is small, the wind velocity state estimates are corrected  whenever the EKF is not dead reckoning (e.g. has an independent velocity or position sensor such as GPS). This behaviour is on by default and cannot be disabled. When the EKF is dead reckoning, the wind states are used as a reference, enabling use of the small angle of sideslip assumption to correct non wind velocity states (eg attitude, velocity, position, etc) and improve navigation accuracy. This behaviour is on by default and cannot be disabled. The behaviour controlled by this parameter is the use of the small angle of sideslip assumption to correct non wind velocity states when the EKF is NOT dead reckoning. This is primarily of benefit to reduce the buildup of yaw angle errors during straight and level flight without a yaw sensor (e.g. magnetometer or dual antenna GPS yaw) provided aerobatic flight maneuvers with large sideslip angles are not performed. The 'always' option might be used where the yaw sensor is intentionally not fitted or disabled. The 'WhenNoYawSensor' option might be used if a yaw sensor is fitted, but protection against in-flight failure and continual rejection by the EKF is desired. For vehicles operated within visual range of the operator performing frequent turning maneuvers, setting this parameter is unnecessary.

parameters.name: EK3_CHECK_SCALE
parameters.description: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.

parameters.name: EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X
parameters.display_name: Ballistic coefficient for X axis drag
parameters.description: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the X body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared.  Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the frontal area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_MCOEF parameter.

parameters.name: EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y
parameters.display_name: Ballistic coefficient for Y axis drag
parameters.description: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the Y body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared.  Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the side area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_MCOEF parameter.

parameters.name: EK3_DRAG_MCOEF
parameters.description: This parameter is used to predict the drag produced by the rotors when flying a multi-copter, enabling estimation of wind drift. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed not speed squared and is produced because some of the air velocity normal to the rotors axis of rotation is lost when passing through the rotor disc which changes the momentum of the airflow causing drag. For unducted rotors the effect is roughly proportional to the area of the propeller blades when viewed side on and changes with different propellers. It is higher for ducted rotors. For example if flying at 15 m/s at sea level conditions produces a rotor induced drag acceleration of 1.5 m/s/s, then EK3_MCOEF would be set to 0.1 = (1.5/15.0). Set EK3_MCOEF to a postive value to enable wind estimation using this drag effect. To account for the drag produced by the body which scales with speed squared, see documentation for the EK3_BCOEF_X and EK3_BCOEF_Y parameters.

parameters.name: EK3_DRAG_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets the amount of noise used when fusing X and Y acceleration as an observation that enables esitmation of wind velocity for multi-rotor vehicles. This feature is enabled by the EK3_BCOEF_X and EK3_BCOEF_Y parameters

parameters.name: EK3_EAS_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the airspeed measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK3_EAS_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in equivalent airspeed measurements used by planes. Increasing it reduces the weighting of airspeed measurements and will make wind speed estimates less noisy and slower to converge. Increasing also increases navigation errors when dead-reckoning without GPS measurements.

parameters.name: EK3_ENABLE
parameters.description: This enables EKF3. Enabling EKF3 only makes the maths run, it does not mean it will be used for flight control. To use it for flight control set AHRS_EKF_TYPE=3. A reboot or restart will need to be performed after changing the value of EK3_ENABLE for it to take effect.

parameters.name: EK3_ERR_THRESH
parameters.display_name: EKF3 Lane Relative Error Sensitivity Threshold
parameters.description: lanes have to be consistently better than the primary by at least this threshold to reduce their overall relativeCoreError, lowering this makes lane switching more sensitive to smaller error differences

parameters.name: EK3_FLOW_DELAY
parameters.description: This is the number of msec that the optical flow measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.

parameters.name: EK3_FLOW_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the optical flow innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK3_FLOW_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise and errors in optical flow measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

parameters.name: EK3_FLOW_USE
parameters.description: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.

Set to about 0.5m less than the amount of negative offset in baro height that occurs just prior to takeoff when lift motors are spooling up. Set to 0 if no ground effect is present.

parameters.name: EK3_MAG_CAL
parameters.description: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states and when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK3_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK3_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. parameters.name: EK3_RNG_USE_SPD

parameters.name: EK3_VELD_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set vertical velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS vertical velocity measurements.

parameters.name: EK3_VELNE_M_NSE
parameters.description: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set horizontal velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS horizontal velocity measurements.

parameters.name: EK3_VEL_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements willbe rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MAX
parameters.description: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when minimum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

parameters.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN
parameters.description: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when maximum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

parameters.name: EK3_WENC_VERR
parameters.description: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when wheel encoder data is being fused.

parameters.name: EK3_WIND_PSCALE
parameters.display_name: Height rate to wind process noise scaler
parameters.description: This controls how much the process noise on the wind states is increased when gaining or losing altitude to take into account changes in wind speed and direction with altitude. Increasing this parameter increases how rapidly the wind states adapt when changing altitude, but does make wind velocity estimation noiser.

parameters.name: EK3_WIND_P_NSE
parameters.description: This state process noise controls the growth of wind state error estimates. Increasing it makes wind estimation faster and noisier.

parameters.name: EK3_YAW_I_GATE
parameters.description: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

parameters.name: EK3_YAW_M_NSE
parameters.description: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

parameters.name: FFT_ATT_REF
parameters.description: FFT attenuation level in dB for bandwidth calculation and peak detection. The bandwidth is calculated by comparing peak power output with the attenuated version. The default of 15 has shown to be a good compromise in both simulations and real flight.

parameters.name: FFT_BW_HOVER
parameters.description: FFT learned bandwidth at hover for the attenuation frequencies.

parameters.name: FFT_ENABLE
parameters.description: Enable Gyro FFT analyser

parameters.name: FFT_FREQ_HOVER
parameters.description: The learned hover noise frequency

parameters.name: FFT_HMNC_FIT
parameters.description: FFT harmonic fit frequency threshold percentage at which a signal of the appropriate frequency is determined to be the harmonic of another. Signals that have a harmonic relationship that varies at most by this percentage are considered harmonics of each other for the purpose of selecting the harmonic notch frequency. If a match is found then the lower frequency harmonic is always used as the basis for the dynamic harmonic notch. A value of zero completely disables harmonic matching.

parameters.name: FFT_HMNC_PEAK
parameters.description: The FFT harmonic peak target that should be returned by FTN1.PkAvg. The resulting value will be used by the harmonic notch if configured to track the FFT frequency. By default the appropriate peak is auto-detected based on the harmonic fit between peaks and the energy-weighted average frequency on roll on pitch is used. Setting this to 1 will always target the highest energy peak. Setting this to 2 will target the highest energy peak that is lower in frequency than the highest energy peak. Setting this to 3 will target the highest energy peak that is higher in frequency than the highest energy peak. Setting this to 4 will target the highest energy peak on the roll axis only and only the roll frequency will be used (some vehicles have a much more pronounced peak on roll). Setting this to 5 will target the highest energy peak on the pitch axis only and only the pitch frequency will be used (some vehicles have a much more pronounced peak on roll).

parameters.name: FFT_MAXHZ
parameters.description: Upper bound of FFT frequency detection in Hz. On smaller vehicles the maximum motor frequency is likely to be significantly higher than for larger vehicles.

parameters.name: FFT_MINHZ
parameters.description: Lower bound of FFT frequency detection in Hz. On larger vehicles the minimum motor frequency is likely to be significantly lower than for smaller vehicles.

parameters.name: FFT_SAMPLE_MODE
parameters.description: Sampling mode (and therefore rate). 0: Gyro rate sampling, 1: Fast loop rate sampling, 2: Fast loop rate / 2 sampling, 3: Fast loop rate / 3 sampling. Takes effect on reboot.

parameters.name: FFT_SNR_REF
parameters.description: FFT SNR reference threshold in dB at which a signal is determined to be present.

parameters.name: FFT_THR_REF
parameters.description: FFT learned thrust reference for the hover frequency and FFT minimum frequency.

parameters.name: FFT_WINDOW_OLAP
parameters.description: Percentage of window to be overlapped before another frame is process. Takes effect on reboot. A good default is 50% overlap. Higher overlap results in more processed frames but not necessarily more temporal resolution. Lower overlap results in lost information at the frame edges.

parameters.name: FFT_WINDOW_SIZE
parameters.description: Size of window to be used in FFT calculations. Takes effect on reboot. Must be a power of 2 and between 32 and 512. Larger windows give greater frequency resolution but poorer time resolution, consume more CPU time and may not be appropriate for all vehicles. Time and frequency resolution are given by the sample-rate / window-size. Windows of 256 are only really recommended for F7 class boards, windows of 512 or more H7 class.
